hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason:
BLOCKED by dcg

Tip: dcg explain "git push --force origin main"

Reason: Force push can destroy remote history. Use --force-with-lease if necessary.

Explanation: git push --force overwrites remote history with your local history. This can permanently destroy commits that others have already pulled, causing data loss for your entire team. Collaborators may lose work, and recovering requires manual intervention from everyone affected.
             
             What can go wrong:
             - Commits others pushed are deleted from remote
             - Team members get diverged histories
             - CI/CD pipelines may reference deleted commits
             
             Safer alternative:
             - git push --force-with-lease: Only forces if remote matches your last fetch
             
             Check remote state first:
               git fetch && git log origin/<branch>..HEAD

Rule: core.git:push-force-long

Retain the affected state in place and report this exact blocked action and reason. Do not move or archive it merely to get around this denial.

When explicit user authorization covers this exact reviewed action, including authorization already given, permit only this command once with: dcg allow-once <DYNAMIC> --single-use

remediation.safeAlternative: Consider using '--force-with-lease' for safer force pushing.
